attributes.body_ja:
「ような気（き）がする」は、「(A) と感（かん）じる」という意味（いみ）を持（も）つ「気（き）がする」に、助動詞（じょどうし）「よう」を付（つ）けて、もっと不確（ふたし）かな気持（きも）ちを加（くわ）えた表現（ひょうげん）です。これは「ちょっと (A) の感（かん）じがする」や「なんとなく (A) のように思（おも）える」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

「よう」は、連体形（れんたいけい）であれば、どのような品詞（ひんし）とも使（つか）うことができます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「気（き）がする」は、「ような気（き）がする」よりもかなり強（つよ）い表現（ひょうげん）になります。そのため、話（はな）し手（て）が自分（じぶん）の考（かんが）えにあまり自信（じしん）がないときや、失礼（しつれい）な印象（いんしょう）を与（あた）えたくないときは、「ような気（き）がする」の方（ほう）がよく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
ような気（き）がする is a phrase that takes the base meaning of 気（き）がする 'to have a feeling that (A)', or 'to give off a vibe that (A)', and adds an extra layer of uncertainty through use of the auxiliary verb よう. This can be understood as meaning 'to have a funny feeling that (A)', or 'to kinda have a feeling that (A)'.

As always, よう must be attached to the attributive form of any word that comes before it.

Caution

気（き）がする is quite a bit stronger than ような気（き）がする, so the latter will often be used when the speaker is not 100% sure about something, and does not want to sound rude.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: All uses of volitional form and よう explained
All the difference uses of よう
Difference between ような気がする and 気がする

attributes.body: ような気がする and そう both express impressions, but with different nuance. ような気がする conveys personal intuition or vague feeling, i.e. something you sense even without clear reason. On the other hand, そう is typically based on observable clues or appearance. In that sense, ような気がする is more subjective and less confident than そう.

second_relatable.title: そう
second_relatable.meaning: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

attributes.body: ように・ような follows the plain form of a verb or adjective, and expresses similarity in a general sense. For example, 春が来たような日 'a day that is like as if spring had come'. ような気がする is a common idiom that uses this pattern, meaning 'have a feeling.' For example, 誰かが来たような気がする ('I have a feeling that someone came.').

Both ような気がする and ぎみ (from 気味) use 気 expressions to convey subtle states or impressions, but with different nuance and usage. ような気がする follows a phrase to express a subjective hunch like 'Have a feeling that (A)', e.g. 来るような気がする 'I have a feeling they'll come.' ぎみ attaches to nouns to express a slight tendency or hint of something observable, often (but not always) negative, e.g. 疲れ気味だ 'I'm feeling a bit tired.'

second_relatable.title: ぎみ
second_relatable.meaning: Looking, Feeling a little, Touch of, Tending to, Slightly

attributes.body: Both ような気がする and 気 use 気 'spirit' expressions to convey subtle states or impressions, but with different nuance and usage. ような気がする follows a phrase to express a subjective hunch like 'Have a feeling that (A)', e.g. 来るような気がする 'I have a feeling they'll come.' 気 itself can be used after verbs mid-sentence or at the end of a sentence to express 'Feel like (doing) (A)', e.g. 行く気満々だよ 'I have a real mind to go!'

Both ような気がする and げ (from 気) use 気 expressions to convey subtle states or impressions, but with different nuance and usage. ような気がする follows a phrase to express a subjective hunch like 'Have a feeling that (A)', e.g. 来るような気がする 'I have a feeling they'll come.' げ attaches to emotion-related stems to describe appearance based on sensory perception, e.g. 悲しげな顔 'A face with a sorrowful air.'

second_relatable.title: げ
second_relatable.meaning: Seemingly, Giving appearance of, [Expresses emotions or feelings]
